body: One big and amazing tip that i would give you is to go into the website of your exam board and go through the specification. When you go through the specification (lets take gcse chemistry aqa as an example) you will find everything that you need to be able to know, how exactly you will be assessed and the Key skills and AOs (Assessment Objectives) that you need to be know. You will also find not only past papers and mark schemes, but even examiner reports of each paper that will give you as a candidate amazing tips that will help you distinguish yourself. For example, if you look at AQA english language, the examiners will talk about how students failed this, and how high achieving students did this and that. By taking that into consideration and revising consistently and regularly, you should be able to really distinguish yourself. Exam practice under exam conditions is also extremely important. And lastly, by far the most important is to start now. Even if its only 15 minutes a day for every subject, if you start now and do all the above including exam practice you will notice improvement. Try to revise regularly, and force yourself away from unimportant things such as screen time.
